title: A capital letter in a search word makes the match case-sensitive (README misses readme.md)
problem: Fuzzy words reach fff-search exactly as typed. In crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs only globs are case-folded (525-529, fold_glob_case 1633-1649) and search_root sends `user` verbatim (637-644). fff builds its matcher with `..Default::default()` (fff-search-0.11.0/src/score.rs:638-647 for files, 434-443 for folders), and the neo_frizbee default is `casing: CaseMatching::Smart` (neo_frizbee-0.13.3/src/lib.rs:326-336): a needle with any capital is matched case-sensitively (its own test at src/matcher/mod.rs:784-792). Only typo tolerance softens this (2 to 6 missing letters, fff-search file_picker.rs:1113). So `Readme` still finds readme.md as a one-typo match, but `README` does not find readme.md or Readme.md, `TODO` does not find todo.txt, and `IMG` finds img_0001.jpg only when some other capital I, M or G happens to be in its path. The engine's own checks all lowercase (words 548-551, strict 570-577, rerank 1511), and docs/manual.md:356 says fuzzy words and quoted words both ignore letter case (manual:998 scopes the case setting to content searches, quoted words and globs). Second consequence: with Letter case set to Ignore Case, the quoted phrase README still cannot find readme.md, because the phrase's words go to fff with their capitals (split_quoted 1587-1588) and the file never reaches contains_phrase (558-563).
proposal: In engine.rs, move the token test now inline in fuzzy_text (1552-1558) into `fn is_fuzzy_word(token: &str) -> bool`, and add `fn fold_word_case(query: &str) -> String` that lowercases every token for which it is true and leaves constraints and globs alone. Apply it where fold_glob_case is applied in Engine::search (line 527): `query: fold_word_case(&fold_glob_case(&query, case))`, under every case setting, since the manual says words ignore case. To keep a typed capital as a ranking preference instead of a filter, keep the typed words (before lowering) and in rerank (1507-1536) add about +10 for each word that has a capital and occurs in the name spelled as typed, so `README` still puts README.md above readme.md. Add a CHANGELOG entry; the manual sentence at 356 then becomes true.
original_test_plan: Engine unit test in engine.rs `mod tests`, same shape as quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter: root with `readme.md`, `pictures/img_0001.jpg`, `a/README.md`, `b/todo.txt`. Assert the names for README contain readme.md and list README.md first, names for IMG == [img_0001.jpg], names for TODO == [todo.txt]; with case = Insensitive the quoted phrase README finds readme.md; with case = Sensitive it returns only README.md. Unit test: fold_word_case of `Main *.RS !Test /Src/` == `main *.RS !Test /Src/`.
original_risks: A lowercase needle loses frizbee's capitalization bonus (score.rs:641-644), so camel-hump queries such as `TE` for TaxExemption rank slightly differently; the rerank bonus only partly replaces it. The query-history lookup key becomes the lowercased string while track_open stores the typed text (engine.rs:1308-1313), so lowercase there too or do the query-history-boost candidate. Not run by the reviewer: the behaviour is derived from reading the three crates, so the new test should be seen failing first.

verifier.claim_check:
The bug claim holds in full; nothing elsewhere handles it. The proposal needs three corrections (see implementation_notes). Cargo was not run, so all of this is from reading the code.

What the code does today:
- `crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:525-529` folds only globs (`fold_glob_case`, 1633-1649). `search_root` sends the words verbatim (637-644) to `fuzzy_search_directories` / `fuzzy_search_mixed` / `fuzzy_search` (696-741).
- The two callers pass the typed query unchanged: `src/finder/mod.rs:1380` and `src/server/mod.rs:407`.
- fff-search-0.11.0 `src/score.rs:638-647` (files) and `434-443` (folders) build `neo_frizbee::Config { ..Default::default() }`. Neither fff-search nor fff-query-parser lowercases the fuzzy needle.
- neo_frizbee-0.13.3 `src/lib.rs:326-336` defaults to `CaseMatching::Smart`; `respects_case_for` (440-448) is true when the needle has any uppercase. Both the prefilter and Smith-Waterman are then built case-sensitive (`src/matcher/algo.rs:64-74`). Its own test (`src/matcher/mod.rs:784-792`) shows `FoO` matching only `FoO` and `xxFoOxx`.
- The typo budget is `(len/4).clamp(2,6)` (`file_picker.rs:1113`, `1200`). So `Readme` finds `readme.md` with one typo, but `README`, `TODO` and `IMG` miss lowercase names.
- The engine's own checks all lowercase: words 548-551, strict 570-577, rerank 1511, `app_hits` 1452, highlight 1690-1699. Apps already ignore case while files do not.
- `docs/manual.md:356` says fuzzy words ignore letter case; `:998` scopes the case setting to content searches, quoted words and globs. The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] covers only globs and quoted words.
- The quoted-phrase consequence is also true: `split_quoted` (1587-1588) passes the phrase's words with their capitals, so under Ignore Case `"README"` never gets `readme.md` back from fff to reach `contains_phrase` (558-563).
- No test pins smart-case for fuzzy words. Every search query in `tests/*.rs` and the engine tests is lowercase, except the quoted `"TaxExemption"` (engine.rs:2034), which still passes because `contains_phrase` filters after fff.

Where the proposal is wrong or incomplete:
1. The proposed ordering assertion fails with the proposed fixture. For the lowered needle `readme`, frizbee gives root `readme.md` the prefix bonus (12) and `a/README.md` only the delimiter bonus (4). fff totals come to about 98 vs 88, rerank takes 3 more off the deeper file, and +10 does not close the gap.
2. `is_fuzzy_word` lifted from `fuzzy_text` skips tokens that fff does read as fuzzy text. Under `MixedSearchConfig` and `DirSearchConfig` (the window's default) path segments are disabled (fff-query-parser `config.rs:221-248`, `parser.rs:302-306`), so `Docs/`, `/Notes/` and `main Src/` stay case-sensitive. So does `Main.rs:42`.
3. The history key is not optional. `track_open` (engine.rs:1290-1315) stores the typed text, while the lookup uses `query.raw_query` (`file_picker.rs:1116-1124`). With `min_combo_count` 0 the boost is +1000 (`score.rs:805`), and it works today for plain queries.
verifier.implementation_notes:
All code changes are in `crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs`.

1. Add `fn fold_word_case(query: &str, path_tokens_are_text: bool) -> String`. Split on whitespace and rejoin with one space, as `fold_glob_case` does.
   - Leave a token alone when its body (after an optional `!`) contains `*`, `?`, `[` or `{`. Those are globs and extensions, and `fold_glob_case` owns them. Its output `*[tT][aA][xX]*` is skipped by the same test.
   - Leave `!` exclusions alone; fff already ignores case for them (`find_case_insensitive_short`).
   - Lowercase everything else, including `name.rs:42` and `git:Modified`.
   - Lowercase tokens that start or end with `/` only when `path_tokens_are_text` is true. In file mode they are PathSegment constraints, which fff already compares ASCII-case-insensitively (`path_slice_eq`); lowering a non-ASCII segment there could break an exact match.
   - Do not reuse the `fuzzy_text` predicate as proposed: it misses folder and `:` tokens.

2. Apply it in `Engine::search` at line 527: `fold_word_case(&fold_glob_case(&query, case), path_text)`, under every case setting.
   - `path_text = req.kind == KindFilter::Folder || (req.kind == KindFilter::Any && !req.files_only)`, mirroring the branches at 696 and 711.
   - The fold runs before `search_root` appends the extension globs and the case-sensitive scope glob, so those stay untouched.
   - `exact` phrases come from `split_quoted` before the fold, so `contains_phrase` still sees the typed capitals.

3. Ranking preference. Before the fold, collect the typed words that have a capital: `fuzzy_text(&query).split_whitespace().filter(|w| w.chars().any(char::is_uppercase))`.
   - In the loop at 581-583, add about +10 per typed word that `display_name(&hit.path)` contains as typed.
   - Do it at the call site or in a small `case_bonus(name, &typed)` helper, so `rerank` keeps its signature and the tests at 1866 and 2245 are untouched.
   - This is a tie-breaker only: it will not beat fff's prefix bonus or a depth difference.

4. History key. In `track_open` (1308-1313), store the query through the same pipeline as search: `split_quoted`, then `fold_glob_case`, then `fold_word_case`, in a shared helper.
   - Otherwise `README` is stored typed and looked up lowered, and the +1000 combo boost that works today is lost.
   - Entries already stored with capitals are orphaned; that is acceptable.

5. Optional: `Engine::list` (1047 and 1064) also passes `q` to fff verbatim for `fff files` / `fff dirs` / `/v1/files?query=`, while matching apps case-insensitively (1090-1101). Apply the same fold there.

6. Docs.
   - `docs/manual.md:356`: say that unquoted words ignore letter case, that a name spelled as typed ranks first, and that quoting is the way to ask for exact case.
   - `CHANGELOG.md`: add a `### Fixed` entry under [Unreleased].

Pitfalls:
- `words` (548) and `needle` (589) are derived from the folded query. That is fine: `highlight` already lowercases.
- `to_lowercase` can change the char count for rare characters such as `İ`; this only matters for the `single_char` check and is negligible.
- A lowered needle turns off fff's `capitalization_bonus` and `matching_case_bonus` (`score.rs:641-644`), so camel-hump queries such as `TE` become plain subsequence matches.
verifier.test_plan:
Engine unit tests in `crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs` `mod tests`, same shape as `quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter` (1987): `Engine::new(EngineOptions { roots, app_dirs: Vec::new(), db_dir: None, watch: false, search: Default::default() })`, `wait_ready(Duration::from_secs(10))`, `engine.search(&SearchRequest { .. })`, and `search_settings` / `set_search_settings` for the case setting. Runs on Linux with no UI.

Fixture: `a/README.md` and `b/readme.md` as siblings at the same depth (not `readme.md` at the root), plus `pictures/img_0001.jpg`, `c/todo.txt`, and a folder `Docs/` holding one file.

Use an unsorted `names` closure, as in `typos_can_be_turned_off` (2060). The sorted one at 2003 would make "README.md first" pass vacuously, because uppercase sorts first. Pass `scope: Some(dir.clone())`, or pick a temp-dir name without the tested letters, because with no scope `strict` (570-577) matches against the whole absolute path.

Assertions with `files_only: true`:
- `README` returns both files, with `README.md` first.
- `IMG` == `[img_0001.jpg]`.
- `TODO` == `[todo.txt]`.
- Case Insensitive: `"README"` returns both.
- Case Sensitive: `"README"` == `[README.md]`, and `"readme"` == `[readme.md]`.

Assertions for the default mixed and folder paths:
- `files_only: false`: `DOCS` returns the `Docs` folder.
- `kind: KindFilter::Folder`: `DOCS/` returns `Docs`.

Pure unit tests:
- `fold_word_case("Main *.RS !Test /Src/ Lib.rs:42", true)` == `"main *.RS !Test /src/ lib.rs:42"`; with `false`, `/Src/` stays.
- `fold_word_case(&fold_glob_case("*Tax* Budget", Insensitive), true)` keeps the folded glob and lowers `Budget`.
- The case bonus on two `RawHit::file` values with equal scores and depth, in the style of `rerank_prefers_name_matches` (1866).

Optional UI check in `tests/finder.rs`, next to `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing`, with the harness in `tests/common/mod.rs`: `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.press(&cmd("f"))`, `ui.type_text("ATLAS")`, then assert `ui.names()` contains `Project Atlas.txt` and `atlas`.

See the new engine test fail before the change.
verifier.risks:
- Capitalised queries return more results and rank differently. The undocumented smart-case narrowing is gone (quoted words remain the documented way to ask for case), and camel-hump queries lose fff's capitalization bonus.
- The +10 bonus is only a tie-breaker. An ordering assertion is fragile unless the fixture keeps depth and path position equal.
- If `track_open` is not folded the same way, the query-history boost silently stops for capitalised queries, and no existing test would catch it. Entries already stored with capitals are orphaned either way.
- Lowering folder tokens in file mode could break non-ASCII segment matches, which is why that part is gated on mixed/folder mode.
- Nothing was run. The behaviour and the score arithmetic (prefix 12 vs delimiter 4, fff totals about 98 vs 88) are derived from reading fff-search 0.11.0 and neo_frizbee 0.13.3.
